implementation_notes: On Kotlin the dominant realization is Koin: startKoin { modules(appModule) } builds the registry, module { single { ... } / factory { ... } } declares implementations and lifetimes, and get<T>() resolves - inside definitions, in a KoinComponent (by inject()) or from a koinInject() call site. The DSL replaces the locator class, and the compiler plugin keeps the graph checked at build time, which recovers the compile-time safety a runtime locator normally loses. Use get<T>() for objects the framework instantiates (Activities, Workers, Compose entry points) and constructor parameters for everything Koin itself creates, so dependencies stay visible wherever that is possible.
pitfalls: get<T>() is a runtime reflective lookup: without the Koin compiler plugin, a missing or misconfigured binding throws NoDefinitionFoundException only when that line executes.
single { } instances live for the container's lifetime, so a singleton that captures an Activity or Context leaks it; scope or factory bindings are required for shorter lifetimes.
koinApplication(...) and startKoin create separate registries - tests that use an isolated Koin instance must not resolve through the global context.

variants.name: JVM ServiceLoader SPI
variants.implementation_notes: Because Kotlin runs on the JVM, java.util.ServiceLoader is available unchanged: providers are listed in META-INF/services/<interface>, loaded lazily, cached, and selected by a rule the caller writes over stream(). It is the right choice for a library that must not bind to a DI framework, for auto-configuration-style discovery (Spring Boot's own kotlin-friendly auto-configuration builds on it) and for plugin jars placed on the class path, and it composes with Koin by registering the discovered providers as bindings in a module.
variants.code_sketch:
val sources: List<PriceSource> =
    ServiceLoader.load(PriceSource::class.java).toList()

val source = sources.maxByOrNull { it.priority }
    ?: error("no PriceSource provider on the class path")
pitfalls: Providers need a public no-arg constructor and an exact fully-qualified name in the service file; a typo raises ServiceConfigurationError while iterating, not at load time.
Do not cache ServiceLoader instances VM-wide (thread context class loader): in application servers and on Android that pins class loaders.
